subject: english-literature
title: From New Criticism to Structuralism
welcome_lead: The mid-twentieth century revolution: close reading meets the science of signs.
meta_desc: New Criticism and structuralism at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have traced the move from autonomous text to system of signs — two foundational mid-century paradigms.

concepts.def: Anglo-American formalist school (Brooks, Ransom, Wimsatt) advocating close reading of the autonomous text.
Wimsatt & Beardsley (1946) — appealing to authorial intention is fallacious; the text is sovereign.
Wimsatt & Beardsley — appealing to reader emotion is also fallacious.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cleanth Brooks's The Well-Wrought Urn (1947) modelled close reading: every metaphor, every paradox earns its keep.

The poem is treated as a verbal icon, prized for unity in tension.
Saussure's Course in General Linguistics (posthumous, 1916) split the sign into signifier (sound-image) and signified (concept). The relation is arbitrary; meaning is differential.

Lévi-Strauss applied Saussurean method to myth, arguing all cultures organise meaning through binary oppositions.

Roland Barthes's early Mythologies (1957) extended this to wrestling matches and steak.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
A theme is the title of the book.

Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.
